project.name: Sale Performance Dashboard
project.description: Static web app for tracking sales targets, revenue schedule, pipeline, and deal activity from CSV files

nodes.name: CONTEXT.md
nodes.summary: Business glossary that defines domain terminology for the Sale Performance Dashboard. Covers four sections: Sales Performance (Deal, Sale Type, Won, Lost, Open Deal), Targets (Sale Target, Achievement, Forecast), Revenue Analysis (Revenue Schedule, Revenue Detail, Revenue Performance, Recurring, One-time, Recurring Target, Contract Period), Lead Analysis (New Deals, Lead, ISO Week), and Data Governance (Mapping, Pipeline Matching, Unmapped, Excluded, Data Quality). Each term includes preferred usage and terms to avoid, ensuring consistent language across the dashboard.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project documentation for Sale Performance Dashboard 2026. Describes a static web app that tracks sales targets, won amounts, revenue schedule, pipeline, deal detail, and new lead activity from CSV files. Documents project structure (index.html, app.js, styles.css, data/, scripts/), offline preview via Node.js preview server at port 4174, test execution for revenue logic, data loading workflow (auto-loads Stage Mapping.csv and Sale Target.csv at startup, deal CSV uploaded via gear button), seven main tabs (Overview, Sales Performance, Revenue Analysis, All Deals, Pipeline Risk, Data Quality, New Deals), global filters (view mode, sale group, period), mapping and counting rules, and core business assumptions.

nodes.name: desktop.ini
nodes.summary: Windows shell folder view state configuration. Sets FolderType to Generic with empty Mode and Vid values. Auto-generated by Windows Explorer and not relevant to application logic.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Main dashboard HTML layout for Sale Performance Dashboard 2026 (lang=th). Loads styles.css, data/dashboard-data.js, scripts/revenue-logic.js, and app.js. Contains: (1) topbar header with title and metaBox; (2) seven-tab navigation (Overview, Sales Performance, Revenue Analysis, All Deals, Pipeline Risk, Data Quality, New Deals); (3) three modal dialogs (Settings with CSV upload and Pipeline Matching matrix, Field Info data-field checker, Deal detail modal); (4) toolbar with two filter cards (Filter มุมมอง: view mode/group/sale/search/New-Renew segment; Filter ช่วงเวลา: Year/Quarter/Month/Range period tabs) and a hidden ISO-Week lead filter card; (5) KPI grid; (6) tab panels for each section with charts, tables, and search inputs using AND/NOT pattern; (7) Revenue Analysis subtabs (Revenue Performance, Revenue Analysis) with collapsible panels for Recurring Target, Revenue Detail, Target Contribution Detail, and Revenue Data Checks.

nodes.name: styles.css
nodes.summary: 2899-line stylesheet providing light/dark theme and responsive layout for the dashboard. Defines CSS custom properties on :root for the light theme (--bg, --surface, --ink, --primary, --won, --lost, --renew, --new-sale, --target, --warn, --danger, --shadow, KPI backgrounds, button states) and overrides on :root[data-theme='dark']. Styles cover: shell/topbar layout, tab navigation, three modal dialogs (settings, field-info, deal), filter cards, KPI grid and summary cards, pipeline matching matrix table, tab panel sections, chart containers (monthly, rank-list, performance, revenue), transaction/AND-NOT search grids, collapsible panels, risk grid, lead/new-deals layout, table-wrap and sortable tables, empty-data banner, and responsive media queries.

nodes.name: push-to-github.cmd
nodes.summary: Windows batch script that delegates to scripts/push-to-github.ps1 via PowerShell. Sets working directory to the script's own location, invokes the PowerShell script with bypass execution policy, and pauses after completion so the user can read output.

nodes.name: start-preview.cmd
nodes.summary: Windows batch script that starts the local offline preview server. Detects node from PATH or falls back to OpenAI Codex bundled node.exe. Launches scripts/preview-server.js on port 4174, opens http://127.0.0.1:4174/ in the browser, and keeps the console window alive for the server process.

nodes.name: Overview Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section showing sales summary. Contains: Target vs Actual by Month bar chart, Team Achievement ranked list, New/Renew Mix grid, Status Mix (Won/Lost/Open), and Top Open Opportunities table.

nodes.name: Sales Performance Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section for sales performance analysis. Contains status filter checkboxes (Won, Commit, Upside, Open, Lost), four performance charts (Renew Sales, New Sales, Total Sales by Sale, Cumulative Monthly Sales), and Transaction Detail table with AND/NOT multi-field search.

nodes.name: Revenue Analysis Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section for revenue recognition and planning. Has two subtabs: Revenue Performance (monthly performance chart vs recurring target, by-sale ranking) and Revenue Analysis (Monthly Revenue Schedule chart, Revenue by Sale Owner, plus collapsible panels for Recurring Target table with CSV export, Revenue Detail with AND/NOT search and CSV export, Target Contribution Detail, Revenue Data Checks).

nodes.name: All Deals Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section displaying all deal detail for the selected period including included, excluded, and unmapped pipeline counting status. Supports AND/NOT multi-field search and shows running total amount.

nodes.name: Pipeline Risk Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section showing open deals with risk signals (overdue, stale, missing expected date, not contacted). Contains Risk Summary grid, Risk by Stage ranked list, and Pipeline Risk Detail table sorted by risk severity and value.

nodes.name: Data Quality Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section for mapping and data governance review. Shows Data Assumptions list, Stage Normalization statistics, and Unmapped Responsible Names table for names that appear in deals but not in Sale Target file.

nodes.name: New Deals Tab
nodes.summary: Dashboard section for lead creation analysis using ISO Week and Created Date. Contains New Deals summary grid, Weekly Lead Trend chart, and Lead Detail by Week table. Uses a dedicated ISO Week filter (from/to week range and lead keyword search).

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: Main application logic for the Sale Performance Dashboard. Contains CSV parsing, state management, filter logic, chart rendering (monthly, team, category, revenue), tab/view switching, deal modal, pipeline risk, revenue analysis, lead tracking, data quality checks, and export functions. The single largest file in the project (~5000 lines).

nodes.name: dashboard-data.js
nodes.summary: Skeleton/seed data file that exposes window.DASHBOARD_DATA. Provides an empty but structurally complete dashboard data object including metadata, months array (2024-2028), stage weights, empty mappings, and quality counters. Loaded before app.js so the app always has a baseline data shape.

nodes.name: Sale Target.csv
nodes.summary: CSV file containing per-salesperson monthly sales targets for renew and new sale types in 2026. Columns include sales name, sale group, annual renew total, monthly renew targets (Jan–Dec), annual new total, and monthly new targets.

nodes.name: Stage Mapping.csv
nodes.summary: CSV file mapping sale groups and sale types to pipeline categories (e.g. Subscription Renew, Corporate, Government Deal Focus, Connectivity). Used to classify deals into the correct pipeline counting buckets per group/type combination.

nodes.name: CHART_STANDARDS.md
nodes.summary: Defines the visual and behavioral standard for Target vs Actual bar charts used throughout the dashboard. Specifies three-layer rendering (target base, actual bar, target outline), tooltip hover rules, color themes per sale type, and gap calculation convention. Applied to Overview monthly chart, Revenue Performance chart, and Revenue Schedule chart.

nodes.name: preview-server.js
nodes.summary: Minimal Node.js HTTP static file server for local development preview. Serves files from the project root with correct MIME types for HTML, CSS, JS, CSV, JSON, and image formats. Configurable port and host via environment variables or CLI args.

nodes.name: push-to-github.ps1
nodes.summary: PowerShell deployment script for committing and pushing the dashboard to GitHub. Validates the git remote, finds git and node executables, supports dry-run via -NoPush flag and auto-confirm via -Yes flag. Includes Thai-language error messages for developer convenience.

nodes.name: revenue-logic.js
nodes.summary: Pure, dependency-injected revenue scheduling library exposed as window.RevenueLogic and as a CommonJS module. Computes per-deal revenue schedules (one-time, recurring, MRR-inferred), allocates contract amounts across months with penny-rounding, and builds a recurring target projection from prior-year revenue schedules.

nodes.name: test-revenue-logic.js
nodes.summary: Node.js test suite for revenue-logic.js using node:assert. Covers one-time billing, recurring billing with contract start/end, expected-date fallback, stage-change-date fallback, MRR mismatch detection, and buildRecurringTargetFromRevenue. Runs standalone via `node test-revenue-logic.js`.

nodes.name: parseCsv
nodes.summary: Parses raw CSV text into an array of objects keyed by header row. Handles quoted fields, escaped quotes, and trims whitespace. Entry point for all CSV data ingestion in the app.

nodes.name: buildDashboardDataFromDeals
nodes.summary: Core data-building function (~260 lines). Takes parsed deal rows and converts them into the full dashboardData shape including facts per sale/month/category, open deals, deal details, stage weights, and quality metrics. Called after CSV upload and on refresh.

nodes.name: buildTargetSalesFromRows
nodes.summary: Parses Sale Target CSV rows into structured sales target objects per salesperson, sale type, year, and month. Applies active mappings to classify each target record into the correct category.

nodes.name: calcScope
nodes.summary: Computes the current filter scope object from global state (selected sale, period, category, search, week). The scope object is passed to all render functions to ensure consistent filtering across views.

nodes.name: filteredDeals
nodes.summary: Returns deals filtered by scope (sale, period/week, category, search, status). Supports options for including won/lost deals and excluding global search. Central filtering function used by all chart and table renderers.

nodes.name: renderMonthlyChart
nodes.summary: Renders the Target vs Actual bar chart by month in the Overview tab. Uses the three-layer bar pattern defined in CHART_STANDARDS.md — target base, actual solid fill, and target outline overlay.

nodes.name: buildRevenueAnalysis
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full revenue analysis for the current scope. Calls revenueScheduleForDeal for each deal, aggregates monthly revenue entries, groups by sale and month, and computes exception and data-check lists.

nodes.name: renderRevenueAnalysis
nodes.summary: Top-level renderer for the Revenue Analysis tab. Delegates to renderRevenueSummary, renderRevenueMonthlyChart, renderRevenueBySale, renderRevenueDetailTable, renderRevenueExceptionTable, and renderRevenuePerformance sub-renderers.

nodes.name: initFilters
nodes.summary: Initializes all filter UI controls — sale selector, period selector, category buttons, week selector, search input. Attaches event listeners that update global state and trigger re-renders.

nodes.name: handleCsvRefresh
nodes.summary: Async handler for CSV file uploads. Reads the uploaded file, determines if it is a deal CSV, target CSV, or mapping CSV, validates rows, rebuilds dashboard data, persists to localStorage, and triggers a full re-render.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Top-level render function. Recomputes scope, updates filter UI, renders meta, KPIs, and delegates to renderActiveTabView. Called whenever state changes.

nodes.name: parseMappingCsv
nodes.summary: Parses Stage Mapping CSV text into a structured mappings object containing pipelineGroupMap, stageMap, dealTypeMap, and salesGroupMap. Handles both the stage-mapping and pipeline-rule formats.

nodes.name: createRevenueLogic
nodes.summary: Factory function that validates required dependency functions and returns the revenue logic API object. Implements dependency injection so the same logic runs in both browser (app.js) and Node.js (tests).

nodes.name: revenueScheduleForDeal
nodes.summary: Core function that computes a deal's complete revenue schedule. Determines billing type (one-time vs recurring), resolves contract start/end from multiple date fields with fallback priority, calculates monthsCount from end date, period field, or MRR inference, and allocates the total amount across months with penny-rounding. Returns entries, months, contractRange, revenueRule, and diagnostic flags.

nodes.name: allocateRevenueAmount
nodes.summary: Distributes a total contract amount evenly across N months using integer-cent arithmetic to eliminate floating-point rounding errors. Remainder cents are distributed to the first months.

nodes.name: buildRecurringTargetFromRevenue
nodes.summary: Projects next-year recurring revenue targets from prior-year deal schedules. Filters won/pre-won recurring deals whose contracts extend into the target year and aggregates their monthly allocations as a baseline target.

tour.title: Project Overview & Domain Context
tour.description: Start here to understand what the dashboard does and why it exists. README.md explains the app's purpose, entry point, and data flow at a high level, while CONTEXT.md provides the business context around sales targets, revenue recognition, and the deal pipeline that drives every design decision in the codebase.

tour.title: Dashboard Layout & Tab Structure
tour.description: index.html is the single-page shell that defines all seven tabs — Overview, Sales Performance, Revenue Analysis, All Deals, Pipeline Risk, Data Quality, and New Deals. Reading it reveals how the UI is structured, where chart containers are anchored, and how the file-upload trigger connects to the rest of the app.

tour.title: Visual Design & Theming System
tour.description: styles.css governs the entire visual language of the dashboard — color palette, typography, card layouts, table styles, and responsive breakpoints. Understanding the theming conventions here helps you interpret how chart and table output from app.js is ultimately presented to the user.

tour.title: Core Application Logic: CSV to Dashboard
tour.description: app.js is the heart of the application. It handles CSV file upload and parsing, applies stage mapping to normalize deal stages, orchestrates calls to revenue-logic.js for recognition calculations, and drives the rendering of all charts and tables across every tab. Trace the data flow from file input event to rendered output here.

tour.title: Revenue Recognition Engine
tour.description: scripts/revenue-logic.js is an isolated business logic module that encapsulates how revenue is recognized across time periods based on deal stage, close date, and contract value. Keeping this logic separate from app.js makes it independently testable and easier to adjust when revenue recognition rules change.

tour.title: Reference Data: Targets, Stage Mapping & Fallback Data
tour.description: These three data files define the static inputs the app depends on. Sale Target.csv holds the sales quota figures used in performance comparisons, Stage Mapping.csv maps raw CRM stage names to normalized categories, and data/dashboard-data.js provides hardcoded fallback data so the dashboard renders meaningfully before any CSV is uploaded.

tour.title: Testing & Local Development Tooling
tour.description: scripts/test-revenue-logic.js is the unit test suite for the revenue recognition engine — reviewing it alongside revenue-logic.js reveals the expected behavior and edge cases the business logic must handle. scripts/preview-server.js is the lightweight Node.js server used to serve the static app locally during development.

tour.title: Deployment & Workflow Scripts
tour.description: The push and start scripts (start-preview.cmd, push-to-github.cmd, scripts/push-to-github.ps1) are the operational glue for the project. They show how a developer starts a local preview session and how the app is published — useful context for anyone setting up the project or contributing changes.
